limits: The producer's calls, read; nothing is re-called.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which gains, losses and runs of homozygosity did the file's producer call?

description: Scan every indexed chromosome of an Affymetrix copy-number container and report what the file itself called: gains, losses and stretches of homozygosity, with their positions, marker counts and spans, plus a per-chromosome summary. Reads the file's own CNState and LOH columns and infers nothing — for a second opinion computed from the log2 ratios, use copy_number_segment. A chromosome that was read and carries nothing is reported as clean, which is a different answer from one that could not be read. NO GENOME BUILD IS ASSUMED: positions are the file's own.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

data_set.description: which data set to scan, by name. Unset is the file's FIRST, which is what the panel opens on.

file.description: which copy-number file in this project, by name. Unset, it is the project's only one — and it refuses rather than guessing when there is more than one.

min_bases.description: ignore any run spanning fewer bases than this. Default 0, for the same reason as min_markers. Note a single-marker run spans 0 bases.

min_markers.description: ignore any run shorter than this many markers. The default counts everything the file called, including single markers, because a reporting floor belongs to the laboratory and not to this tool.

name: copy_number_findings

bed.description: the same calls as a UCSC BED track, ready for IGV, the UCSC browser or bedtools: 0-based half-open, one row per finding, colored by kind through itemRgb, with the producer's confidence in the score column (0 where the file states none) and the genome build on the `track db=` line when the container names one. The JSON `findings` above carry the file's own inclusive marker positions; this output is the same calls converted once, by the same writer the Export panel uses

chromosomes.description: per chromosome: markers read, and the counts and spans of gains, losses and LOH runs

findings.description: every gain, loss and stretch of homozygosity, as the file called them: kind, chromosome, startPosition, endPosition, markerCount, bases, and — where the file states them — state and stateLabel (the copy-number state; absent on an LOH finding, which is not a copy-number call), confidence (the producer's own, 0..1) and mixture (mosaic fraction, signed as the file signs it, so a mosaic loss and a mosaic gain stay distinguishable). No cytoband: naming a band needs a genome build, and this node is given none

source.description: which route answered: `segments` means the producer's own segment calls, which is what a CYCHP written by ChAS carries; `markers` means the per-marker state columns, which is what a CNCHP carries. Different provenance for the same question, so a pipeline comparing two files can tell which it got

summary.description: what was found, across how many chromosomes and markers
